correctness.rationale: The conclusion is correct for the specified F5 models, not the Kummer quotient. The ground-field blowup identity requires compatible arithmetic models: BCCO Theorem 4.3 itself works geometrically, while Lemmas 4.1 and 5.1 give descended centers at I5×I5 and compatible III×III resolutions. At III×III the factors of u^4−v^4 are F5-linear and the last node has split tangent quadric cd=u²+v². The local small-resolution chain has three rational lines. For the IV cusp put s=t+2 and use the resolution chart y=xv, s=xw: the equation begins v²=4x+3w² in the terms determining x to order two, hence the initial base parameter is w(v²−3w²)/4. Since 3^(-1)=2, the two identical factors in the self-product give the actual descended cubic w(w²−2v²)=w'(w'²−2v'²), not the F25 split-chart cubic mistakenly used over F5. At infinity the nodal Weierstrass point has nonsplit tangent cone y²=2(x−1)²; reflection of the five-cycle fixes one node. Independently enumerated Weierstrass and cubic points with polynomial arithmetic over F5, F25 and F125 and the verified geometric corrections: Y=256,41426,2031376; cubic=31,801,15751; B=336,43576,2063376; small resolution=306,42926,2047626 (python3 /workspace/branches/independent_finite_fields.py). The frozen checker was inspected, not run. Hard Lefschetz on projective B and purity give trace 1075 at F25, saturating 43 eigenvalues of modulus 25, so their F5 roots are ±5. Trace 35 over F5 gives multiplicities 25 and 18. Blowing down the rational P1 removes one +5 in H2 and one +25 in H4; odd Betti numbers remain zero. Alternating determinants prove the full stated zeta for all degrees, without assuming semisimplicity from the trace check.
